The company develops software for its phones, distributed through its V-Appstore, with iManager included in their proprietary, [[Android (operating system)|Android]]-based operating system, [[Origin OS]] in [[mainland China]], and currently discontinued [[Funtouch OS]] elsewhere. It has 40,000 employees, with 10 R&D centers in [[Shenzhen]], [[Dongguan]], [[Nanjing]], [[Beijing]], [[Hangzhou]], [[Shanghai]], [[Xi'an]], [[Taipei]], [[Tokyo]], and [[San Diego]].{{cite web |title= A Look Inside: Vivo Tokyo R&D Center |url= https://techplugged.com/a-look-inside-vivo-tokyo-rd-center |website= TechPlugged |date=22 January 2022 |access-date=8 February 2022}}{{cite web |title= Vivo Bolsters its Global Manufacturing Network with Two More Production Bases |url=https://techuncode.com/vivo-bolsters-its-global-manufacturing-network-with-two-more-production-bases |website=Techuncode |last=Anthony |first=Ogbonna |date=11 August 2021 |access-date=8 February 2022}} == History == Since its founding in 2009, Vivo has expanded its global market, serving over 400 million users with its mobile products and services in over 60 countries and regions.{{cite web |title=Vivo among Top 3 in Market Share for the Philippines, Malaysia, and India |url=https://pandaily.com/vivo-among-top-3-in-market-share-for-the-philippines-malaysia-and-india/ |website=Pandaily |access-date=28 February 2022 |date=16 December 2021}} In 2017, Vivo entered the smartphone market in [[Taiwan]], [[Hong Kong]], [[Macau]], [[Russia]], [[Brunei]], [[Cambodia]], [[Laos]], [[Sri Lanka]], [[Bangladesh]], and [[Nepal]], [[Vietnam]].{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-04-24 |title=Điện thoại pin trâu, sạc 23 phút dùng cả ngày gây sốt dân công nghệ |url=https://vtcnews.vn/dien-thoai-pin-trau-sac-23-phut-dung-ca-ngay-gay-sot-dan-cong-nghe-ar939497.html |access-date=2026-02-26 |website=Báo điện tử VTC News |language=vi}}[http://www.dealstreetasia.com/stories/vivo-mobile-enters-myanmar-market-4454/ Vivo Mobile enters Myanmar market]. com o nome Jovi|work=G1|date=April 8, 2025|access-date=April 8, 2025}} === Marketing === In October 2015, Vivo became the [[title sponsor]] of the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL) under a two-year deal starting in the [[2016 Indian Premier League|2016 season]].[http://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/75240/vivo-bags-indian-premier-league-title-sponsorship-for-two-years Vivo bags IPL title sponsorship for two years]. Retrieved on 2017-01-03.[http://www.thequint.com/sports/2015/10/27/vivo-formally-announces-partnership-with-bcci-as-ipl-sponsor Vivo Formally Announces Partnership With BCCI as IPL Sponsor]. Thequint.com (2015-10-27). Retrieved on 2017-01-03. In July 2017, the deal was extended until 2022.{{Cite news|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/india/content/story/1106833.html|title=vivo retains IPL title rights till 2022 after massive bid|work=Cricinfo|access-date=2017-06-27|language=en}} However, in response to the [[2020–2021 China–India skirmishes]] between India and China, the [[Board of Control for Cricket in India]] (BCCI) was criticised in India for allowing a Chinese company to be the title sponsor of the league. Vivo and BCCI mutually agreed to suspend the deal for the 2020 season, with a clause to resume it next season.{{Cite web|title=IPL title sponsor: Dream 11 replaces Vivo as IPL 2020 title sponsor, to pay BCCI Rs 222 crore|url=https://www.timesnownews.com/sports/article/ipl-title-sponsor-dream-11-replaces-vio-as-ipl-2020-title-sponsor-to-pay-bcci-250-crore/638828|access-date=2020-08-18|website=www.timesnownews.com|date=18 August 2020 |language=en}} In June 2017, Vivo reached a sponsorship deal with [[FIFA]] to become the official smartphone brand of the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]] and [[2022 FIFA World Cup]]s.{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2017/6/2/15728884/vivo-world-cup-fifa-china-smartphone-sponsor|title=vivo wants you to know its name so much it's sponsoring the World Cup|website=The Verge|access-date=4 June 2017|date=2 June 2017}} The company also signed a deal with [[UEFA]] as an official partner of the [[UEFA Euro 2020]] and [[UEFA Euro 2024]],{{Cite web|last=UEFA.com|date=2020-10-20|title=Vivo becomes official partner of UEFA EURO 2020 and 2024|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/0262-10a7e6283cfe-39c5c148caf4-1000--vivo-becomes-official-partner-of-uefa-euro-2020-and-2024/|access-date=2020-11-26|website=[[UEFA]]|language=en}} and became a title sponsor of India's [[Pro Kabaddi League]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/other-sports/pro-kabaddi-signs-record-five-year-deal-with-vivo/story-lo6ZEnSTzYXM8g3CSf8sqN.html|title=Pro Kabaddi league: STAR Sports signs record five-year deal with vivo|date=2017-05-08|work=Hindustan Times|access-date=2017-09-04|language=en}} Vivo has a sponsorship deal with the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] in China, with [[Golden State Warriors]] player [[Stephen Curry]]. He endorses the brand in China and the Philippines.{{cite web|url=http://adage.com/article/cmo-strategy/stephen-curry-endorsing-a-chinese-smartphone-brand/308596/|title=Why Stephen Curry Is Plugging a Chinese Smartphone|author=Doland, Angela|date=2017-04-24|work=Advertising Age|access-date=2017-08-17}} In March 2024, Vivo became the main sponsor for [[Nepal Idol]]. They became the official smartphone brand for the television series.{{cite web|url=https://theannapurnaexpress.com/story/47752/#:~:text=Vivo%20mobile%20is%20the%20main,fifth%20edition%20of%20Nepal%20Idol.|work=The Annapurna Express|title=Nepal Idol Season 5 starts in March 7|date=2024-02-28}} ==Controversy == === IMEI and build number controversy in India === In June 2020, the cybercrime unit of [[Meerut]] Police revealed that more than 13,500 Vivo smartphones used in India were operating with the same [[International Mobile Equipment Identity|IMEI number]]. The IMEI number is a 15-digit code intended to be unique to each mobile device, which can be used for tracking criminals or stolen mobile phones. By using the same IMEI number for multiple devices, Vivo may have hindered police efforts to track criminals or stolen devices. In 2017, the [[Telecom Regulatory Authority of India]] issued a statement requiring all mobile devices to have a unique IMEI number. Failure to comply would be considered tampering and could result in a fine or imprisonment for up to three years. The events led to the police filing a case against Vivo and its service center. The issue reportedly came to light when a police officer submitted his mobile phone to the staff at the cybercrime unit for examination, as the phone was not functioning properly despite being repaired at a Vivo service center in Meerut. The cybercrime unit discovered that the IMEI number of the device differed from the one printed on the box. They then forwarded the IMEI number to an unidentified [[Telephone company|telecommunications company]] that provides services for the handset and requested the relevant data. The company informed them that as of 24 September 2019, the same IMEI number had been associated with 13,557 mobile phones across different states in the country. The Meerut police reportedly issued a notice to Vivo India's nodal officer, Harmanjit Singh, under Section 91 of the CrPC and also registered a case under [[Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code]].{{Cite web|date=2020-06-05|title=More than 13,500 Vivo phones running on same IMEI, Meerut police files case|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/technology/mobile-tabs/vivo-phones-same-imei-13500-6444369/|access-date=2020-06-06|website=The Indian Express|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=Banerjee|first=Prasid|date=2020-06-05|title=Police confirms phones with same IMEI number were made by Vivo|url=https://www.livemint.com/technology/tech-news/police-confirms-phones-with-same-imei-number-were-made-by-vivo-11591367089206.html|access-date=2020-06-06|website=Livemint|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=June 2020|first=Jitendra Soni 05|title=Over 13000 Vivo phones found to be using same IMEI number|url=https://www.techradar.com/news/over-13000-vivo-phones-found-to-be-using-same-imei-number|access-date=2020-06-06|website=TechRadar India|date=5 June 2020 |language=en}}{{Cite web|date=5 June 2020|first=Piyush|last=Rai|title=Cop dropped off phone for repairs, 'unique' IMEI found active on 13,500 phones|newspaper=The Times of India|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/cop-dropped-off-phone-for-repairs-unique-imei-found-active-on-13500-phones/articleshow/76206203.cms|access-date=2020-06-06|language=en}} ===Tax evasion allegation in India=== The [[Directorate of Revenue Intelligence]] of India (DRI) raided the offices of Vivo in July 2022 and accused the company of tax evasion. The company allegedly remitted almost half of its turnover out of India.{{Cite news |date=7 July 2022 |title=Vivo India remitted about 50% of its turnover to China to avoid taxes: ED |work=Business Standard |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/vivo-india-remitted-about-50-of-its-turnover-to-china-to-avoid-taxes-ed-122070700831_1.html}} The [[Enforcement Directorate]] also blocked the bank accounts of the company to prevent further money laundering.{{Cite web |title=India raids vivo offices over money laundering allegations |url=https://techcrunch.com/2022/07/06/india-raids-vivo-offices-over-money-laundering-allegations/ |access-date=2022-07-30 |website=TechCrunch |date=6 July 2022 |language=en-US}} The agency also found that some top executives of Vivo who are Chinese had incorporated 23 shell companies in India, with the help of a [[Chartered Accountant (India)|Chartered Accountant]], Nitin Grg. "These (23) companies are found to have transferred huge amounts of funds to Vivo India. Further, out of the total sale proceeds of Rs 1,25,185 crore, Vivo India remitted Rs 62,476 crore or almost 50 percent of the turnover out of India, mainly to China", the ED said in a statement.{{Cite web |title=DRI Says Vivo India Evaded Customs Duty Worth Rs 2,217 Crore |url=https://thewire.in/government/dri-says-vivo-india-evaded-customs-duty-worth-rs-2217-crore |access-date=2023-05-01 |website=The Wire}}{{Cite web |date=2022-08-03 |title=DRI detected customs evasion worth over ₹2.21 crore by Vivo India: Govt |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/technology/dri-detected-customs-evasion-worth-over-rs-2-21-crore-by-vivo-india-govt-101659530000572.html |access-date=2023-05-01 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}} In October 2023, the Enforcement Directorate arrested the head of administration of Vivo India on money laundering charges.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2023-10-12 |title=India arrests Chinese smartphone executive in fraud probe |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/10/12/tech/vivo-india-arrest-intl-hnk/index.html |access-date=2023-10-13 |website=[[CNN]] |language=en}} ==Notes== {{notelist|2}} ==References== {{reflist|2}} ==External links== {{Portal|Technology|Companies}} * {{Official website}} {{Vivo}} {{Electronics industry in China}} {{Major mobile device companies}} [[Category:Vivo (technology company)| ]] [[Category:Mobile phone manufacturers]] [[Category:Mobile phone companies of China]] [[Category:Electronics companies of China]] [[Category:Companies based in Dongguan]] [[Category:Electronics companies established in 2009]] [[Category:Chinese brands]] [[Category:Chinese companies established in 2009]] [[Category:Privately held companies of China]] [[Category:Multinational companies headquartered in China]]
